{{Nihongo|'''Akio Hattori'''|服部 晶夫|Hattori Akio|extra=born in Tokyo in 1929,<ref>Birthdate from [http://www.worldcat.org/identities/np-hattori,%20akio$1929 Worldcat author information], retrieved 2013-12-22.</ref> died on 25 August 2013 due to [[Salivary gland tumour|submandibular gland cancer]].<ref name="asahi">{{citation | title = Hattori Akio-san shikyo|trans-title=Mr.Masao Hattori has died | url=http://www.asahi.com/shimen/articles/TKY201308290610.html |archive-date=2013-12-24|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131224105627/http://www.asahi.com/shimen/articles/TKY201308290610.html| language = ja | date=2013-08-30 | newspaper=[[Asahi Shimbun]] }}</ref> |oclc=}} was a Japanese mathematician working in [[algebraic topology]] who [[mathematical proof|proved]] the [[Hattori–Stong theorem]]. Hattori was the president of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]] in 1989–1991.<ref name="asahi"/><ref>{{citation | url=http://mathsoc.jp/pamph/history/ICM90/sugaku4301001-008.pdf | title= ICM-90 Tokushu-go: dai 21-kai kokusai sugakusha kaigi ni tsuite |last= Komatsu |first= Hikosaburo | language = ja | page= 7 |trans-title=Feature:ICM-90; On the 21st ICM.| access-date=2013-09-01 }}</ref>

Hattori received a Doctorate in Science from the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1959<ref>{{cite book|title= Faiba bandoru no De Rham kohomoroji ni okeru supekutoru keiretsu |trans-title= Spectrum series in De Rham cohomology of fiber bundle|language= ja|last=Hattori|first=Akio|publisher= University of Tokyo |year=1959}}</ref> with [[Shokichi Iyanaga]] as his advisor. He then joined the faculty of the University of Tokyo.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Morita | first1=Shigeyuki | last2=Matsumoto | first2=Shigenori | title=Mathematical contributions of Professor Akio Hattori | mr=1080878 | year=1990 | journal=Journal of the Faculty of Science. University of Tokyo. Section IA. Mathematics | issn=0040-8980 | volume=37 | issue=3 | pages=i–iv | url=http://repository.dl.itc.u-tokyo.ac.jp/dspace/bitstream/2261/55361/2/jfs370217_revised2013sep.pdf | access-date=2014-04-21 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140423053806/http://repository.dl.itc.u-tokyo.ac.jp/dspace/bitstream/2261/55361/2/jfs370217_revised2013sep.pdf | archive-date=2014-04-23 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Between 1966 and 1968 Hattori worked as a visiting scholar at both [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Yale University]].

After retirement from University of Tokyo, Hattori was invited to teach at [[Meiji University]] from 1991<ref>{{cite journal|title= Oshirase : Hattori Akio-sensei no goseikyo wo itamu|trans-title=Notice: Mourn for the passing of Dr. Akio Hattori|language= ja|last= Furuta|first= Mikio|journal= Science Department Bulletin, Graduate School of Science |volume=45 |number=3 |page= 15|date=September 2013|url= https://repository.dl.itc.u-tokyo.ac.jp/?action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=28930&item_no=1&attribute_id=19&file_no=1 |publisher= Faculty of Science, University of Tokyo |access-date= 2018-06-13|oclc=997304695}}</ref><ref name="MEXT"/> to 1999,<ref name="MEXT">{{cite web|url=https://nrid.nii.ac.jp/en/nrid/1000080011469/|title=HATTORI Akio : Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) Database|publisher=[[Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology]] |access-date=2018-06-13}}</ref> when they opened mathematics major in 1989. Professor Hiroko Morimoto invited Drs. Akio Hattori and Hiroshi Fujita from the University of Tokyo, and Dr. Shiro Goto from [[Nihon University]] joined to launch a research and educational system for algebra, geometry and analytics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sūgaku kyōshitsu-dayori : Meijidaigaku rikōgakubu sūgakka|trans-title= Mathematics Class Newsletter : Department of mathematics, Meiji University Faculty of Science and Technology |language=ja|last=Gotō|first=Shirō|url= http://mathsoc.jp/publication/tushin/1701/meiji.pdf}}</ref>
